title: The Signal Lab
summary: The Signal Lab (the Signal panel) is a node-graph sound designer: wire sources through processing to a Sink, play the result live, then save it, render it or put it on the timeline.
alternateQueries: How do I make a sound from scratch?

blocks.text: The Signal Lab forges sounds from oscillators, filters, motion and envelope shaping. You place nodes on a canvas and connect them with wires. Audio flows along the wires from sources to the Sink, which is the output.

The panel has a title and status line, a Compile button, a Properties column on the left (the signal's name and description, and a Variables list), and the node canvas. Scopes and analyzers open as separate views.
The Signal Lab plays live through the audio engine: press Play with the Signal Lab focused and you hear the graph as you edit it. It needs no track on the Tracker.
The Signal Lab is Station's one DSP graph; there is no separate patch editor. Signals can be saved to the library, rendered into the project as a WAV, or placed on the timeline as Signal clips.
